subject: Kappa model persistent tail latency — request to quarantine traffic and propose credit offset
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: FastCommerce SRE <sre@fastcommerce.com>, Liam O'Reilly <liam@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kappa model persistent tail latency — request to quarantine traffic and propose credit offset

Hi Liam / FastCommerce SRE team,

We observed a sustained increase in tail latency (p95) for model "kappa" v2.3 starting ~2027-06-17 22:00 UTC. This is not a single blip — the p95 has been elevated for ~10+ hours across your production traffic and we're continuing to see degraded response times on requests with longer contexts.

Quick facts:
- Affected model: kappa v2.3 (rolled 2027-06-17 21:45 UTC)
- Symptom: persistent p95 uplift ~2.5x baseline on requests >512 tokens
- Impact: degraded UX on batch document-summarization flows; error rate unchanged

We recommend the following immediate containment steps (provisional):
1) Quarantine production traffic for model:kappa:v2.3 (route a copy to diagnostic pool, stop new traffic).
2) Pin your tenant traffic to kappa:v2.2 (fallback variant) for a controlled window while we diagnose.
3) Lodge a temporary canary hold for any automated rollouts to prevent subsequent rollouts until cleared.

Because this rollout happened recently and your SLA p95 commitment covers latency, we'd like to discuss a short credit offset for the affected window while we resolve root cause. I propose a provisional 10% usage credit for the impacted 48-hour window, to be finalized once we have a postmortem.

Attachments: kappa-p95-trends.csv (sampleed p95 across regions), runbook link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/kappa-incident-20270618

Can you confirm: 1) whether you want immediate pin to v2.2, and 2) whether a 4-hour quarantine window to start is acceptable while we assemble a deeper mitigation plan?

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com

From: FastCommerce SRE <sre@fastcommerce.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Liam O'Reilly <liam@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kappa model persistent tail latency — request to quarantine traffic and propose credit offset

Thanks Connor — we saw the same on our side and have started collecting head and tail traces.

We can accept an initial 4-hour quarantine and pin to v2.2 if Redwood approves and provides a clear rollback path. Before we do that, can you confirm:
- Whether the quarantine will preserve existing sessions/ongoing requests (we prefer graceful drain)
- Whether the pin will be tenant-scoped (only FastCommerce)

We attached a short log extract that shows elevated request durations from our edge (excerpt). We also need evening-hours coverage from Redwood's Infra team if the investigation goes beyond the quarantine window.

On Fri, 18 Jun 2027 at 08:12 Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com> wrote:
> We observed a sustained increase in tail latency (p95) for model \"kappa\" v2.3 starting ~2027-06-17 22:00 UTC...

--
FastCommerce SRE Team
sre@fastcommerce.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Kappa model persistent tail latency — internal coordination

Connor — looping infra and product ops.

Summary of what I see from the telemetry:
- Canary runs for v2.3 passed on short-sequence workloads but we see a systematic increase in attention time for long-sequence paths (512+ tokens).
- Kernel hotspot appears when sequence length expands in a specific code path (we have a profiling snapshot).

Suggested internal plan (needs your sign-off to communicate):
1) Approve immediate tenant-scoped pin to kappa:v2.2 for FastCommerce only. Pin implementation: create routing override for their tenant ID, TTL 24 hours (manual review), graceful drain over 5 minutes.
2) Open quarantine: route v2.3 traffic into a diagnostic pool (no customer traffic) while tags stay in place.
3) Canary hold: freeze v2.3 global rollouts until root-cause PR validated and ops-signed.
4) Credit proposal: recommend starting with 15% provisional usage credit for the impacted 48-hour window; marketing can finalize language.

Attachments: kappa-p95-trends.csv (attached).

If you want, Ben can draft the customer note and the credit language.

Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Reliability
kimberly@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam@fastcommerce.com>, FastCommerce SRE <sre@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kappa model persistent tail latency — request to quarantine traffic and propose credit offset

Thanks Liam — appreciate the quick signal.

Redwood plan (proposed, needs your go-ahead):
- Initiate a tenant-scoped pin for FastCommerce to kappa:v2.2 immediately. This will be a routing override only for your tenant ID; TTL set to 24 hours and we will not auto-extend without your consent. Graceful drain will be applied (5 minutes).
- Quarantine kappa:v2.3 in a diagnostic pool for 4 hours to gather traces, with the option to extend if necessary. No customer traffic will be routed to quarantined instances.
- Canary hold: prevent any further automated rollouts for kappa until we complete verification.

Credit proposal: we can apply a provisional 10% usage credit for FastCommerce for the 48 hours covering the incident window (proposal subject to contracts/finance review). Kimberly recommended 15%; I'm proposing 10% as a starting point to expedite approvals. If you accept the containment plan, I'll route the credit proposal through our contracts team for sign-off and get a final DocuSign.

Next steps: please reply with 'APPROVE-PIN' if you'd like us to enact the pin and the 4-hour quarantine now. If you need adjustments to the drain window or credit amount, tell me and we'll adapt.

Attachments: kappa-containment-runbook.pdf

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com

From: contracts@fastcommerce.com
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Reilly <liam@fastcommerce.com>, FastCommerce SRE <sre@fastcommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kappa model persistent tail latency — contractual confirmation and credit cap

Connor / Kimberly,

We can accept the proposed containment (tenant-scoped pin to v2.2 + 4-hour quarantine) subject to two items:
1) Cap on credits: we can agree to the provisional credit, but request a firm cap of 12 hours of equivalent usage credit (we don't want open-ended percentages without a cap).
2) Postmortem: Redwood to deliver a technical postmortem within 72 hours with a remediation timeline and validation plan.

If Redwood confirms those two items publicly in writing we'll send a quick approval email and instruct our procurement team to expect the DocuSign for the adjusted credit amount.

Please reply here with the cap acknowledgment and postmortem commitment.

Thanks,
FastCommerce Contracts
contracts@fastcommerce.com
